plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree covered in clouds of delicate, slightly fragrant blossoms that open before the leaves emerge. Widely planted in parks and along streets and rivers across temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to late April in the Northern Hemisphere; later in cooler or high-elevation areas such as northern Japan and northern Europe
plants.location: Japan, Korea, Washington D.C. (USA), and temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The cherry blossom festival tradition, hanami, dates back over a thousand years in Japan, and the Yoshino cherry trees in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, including single, double, fringed, and parrot forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to May in the Northern Hemisphere, peaking in mid-to-late April in the Netherlands
plants.location: Netherlands, Northern Europe, North America, and temperate gardens worldwide; wild ancestors from Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the 17th century Dutch 'Tulip Mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous North American tree whose bare branches and even trunk are studded with clusters of pea-like magenta-pink flowers before heart-shaped leaves unfold. Important early nectar source for native bees.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, northern Mexico, and southern Ontario; woodland edges and gardens
plants.funFact: The flowers are edible and have a slightly tart flavor, and they grow directly from the trunk and old branches, a trait called cauliflory.

plants.name: Watsonia borbonica
plants.description: A cormous perennial from South Africa producing tall spikes of tubular flowers above sword-shaped leaves. Though its main bloom is spring in the Southern Hemisphere, related species of the Iridaceae family flower in the autumn months in some cooler coastal areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in its native range, with some Watsonia species flowering in autumn, including April, in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa; also naturalized in Australia and parts of California
plants.funFact: Watsonias are adapted to fire-prone fynbos and often bloom profusely after a burn, stimulated by the nutrient-rich ash and increased light.
